ac1_history.engine: after the optimisation: tied scores ordered by float summation order (store-swap run, commit 3c43bab)
final: deterministic tie-break (scores equal to 9 decimals, then lowest component id)

meta.note_engine_versions: every table in this file (methods, headline, repeat/novel, poisoning, change evidence, store swap) comes from the final engine; see ac1_history for how the top-1 count moved: 1379 -> 1380 -> 1376 of 1800

pagerank.note: chosen restart probability sits on the grid boundary (0.5). The engine's own dev grid size is not recorded in the repo, so this budget is a stated choice, not a copy of it.

headline.baseline_choice_note: best non-oracle baseline by AC@1 on this split (favours the baseline)

repeat_vs_novel.definition: repeat = this incident's (root, entry alerting service) pair occurred in an earlier incident at the same company

false_edges.note: false = learned edge absent from the true graph (comes from a wrong postmortem); confirmed = got a second confirmation; decayed = dropped by the reweight rule
false = learned edge absent from the true graph (comes from a wrong postmortem); confirmed = got a second confirmation; decayed = dropped by the reweight rule

placebo_stress.note: the simulator's wrong postmortems keep a true causal chain, so the real run creates no false edges; the placebo run (random root and random edges) is the stress case where every learned edge is a candidate false edge

ops.note: single-process wall-clock per verdict (graph snapshot + walk); HydraDB latency is measured by the store-swap run when a HydraDB node is reachable

tokens_per_verdict.note: ghostwalk and tfidf call no model. No LLM baseline has been run (it needs an API key and spend), so there is no number for it

hydradb_latency.node: HydraDB v0.4.0 published image, docker, loopback

cached.note: in the online loop every incident follows a learner write, so every verdict is a MISS; hits happen when several alerts arrive between postmortems

in_db.note: 2 MSpaths + 4 small reads (components, aliases, shortcuts, revision); no edge read

llm_tokens.definition: language-model tokens spent per verdict. Neither the walk nor the TF-IDF search calls a model, so both are 0 by construction (no LLM is imported anywhere in the verdict path)

ops.checks_definition: 1-based rank of the true root in the ranked list (absent from the list = list length + 1)

hydradb_online_loop_test.backend: HydraDB v0.4.0, local node in docker (loopback)

change_evidence.grid_edge_note: best GAMMA at grid edge; larger values unexplored
change_evidence.note: the DEV optimum (gamma 1, tau 30) sits on the grid corner, so a larger weight was not tried
change_evidence.helps_only_when: helps only when the root's own change is common: reliable gain (95% CI above 0) for p_root in [0.5, 0.8]; at p_root=0.2 the gain is +0.4 pts with a CI that includes 0. Distractor noise up to r_noise=5 does not remove it at p_root=0.5.

inmemory.description: in-process dict graph (the parity-tested stand-in for HydraDB)

hydradb.description: HydraDB v0.4.0 (published image): graph in HydraDB, weighted paths and counters read back every verdict

pg_cte.description: Postgres tables, multi-hop reach by recursive CTE

pgvector.description: pgvector: nearest embedded postmortem text names the root (no graph)

store_swap.note: ΔAC@1 is measured against HydraDB. Latency is the whole verdict (snapshot read + walk) per incident. Embeddings are feature-hashed bags of words (no model).

engine.note: store swap run with the final engine; HydraDB, in-memory and Postgres-CTE give the identical top-1 count

meta.note: both databases in docker on one machine, loopback

postgres_verdict.definition: two batched recursive CTEs per verdict (down from the alerting services, up from every candidate), then the same walk()

hydradb.status: not run at scale: HydraDB is reachable, but a write costs about 65 ms (one request per edge), so loading 1,000 or 5,000 services through it was not benchmarked. Its latency on the 30 TEST companies is in ops.hydradb_latency

gate.rule: stop if p95 at 1,000 services < 100 ms; port walk()'s Bellman-Ford to Rust only if p95 at 5,000 services > 250 ms

hygiene: adjacency built once per graph revision and cached (GraphState.invalidate on every learner write)
per-verdict memo of (1 - miss rate); loop constants hoisted; the candidate loop visits only the services a candidate reaches and charges unreachable alerting services their closed-form ln(eps)
HydraDB path costs (-ln w) are already stored with w on every write; UNWIND batching of path queries was NOT done (needs a node and a response parser)
no per-request JSON reload: results.json is re-read only when its mtime changes
